desc:
Order fraud flags for online store owners mark risky orders for a person to check before they ship. Ecom Swift LLC sets up clear rules in your store, tags the orders that trigger them and sends you the reasons, so you decide to ship, hold or cancel.

## What are order fraud flags?

Order fraud flags are simple warning signs attached to an order. A rule looks at details such as the billing country, the shipping address, the quantity and the shipping speed, and adds a tag when something looks unusual. The flag does not decide anything. It tells a human that this order deserves a closer look.

This differs from automatic blocking. A blocking system can turn away honest customers with an unusual address or a large gift order. A flag system keeps the decision with you, and it keeps a record of why an order was marked.

## Why small stores need a second pair of eyes

A single fraudulent order costs more than the product. You may lose the goods, pay shipping, pay a dispute fee and lose time answering the payment provider. For a small store, a handful of chargebacks can dominate a month.

Most owners check suspicious orders by memory and instinct, and that works until the store gets busy. Orders arrive at night, staff change and patterns go unnoticed, such as five attempts from one address with different cards. Written rules catch the same signs every time, and they show the reason, which helps you decide quickly instead of studying every order.

## What a good flag system includes

- Rules written in plain words, so you can read, question and change them.
- A check for billing and shipping countries that do not match.
- A check for unusually large quantities of a single item.
- A check for rushed shipping on a customer's first order.
- A check for repeated attempts from the same address, email or device details your store records.
- A tag on every flagged order, visible in your order list.
- An email alert that lists which rules triggered and why.
- A review queue where flagged orders wait with a status and a decision note.
- A risk level of low, medium or high, so urgent orders rise to the top.
- An evidence checklist for disputes, so you can respond quickly if a chargeback arrives.

## How we build it

We begin by asking what has gone wrong before: past chargebacks, canceled orders and orders you were unsure about. We also ask what your normal orders look like, because a store that sells bulk supplies has different normal quantities from one that sells single gifts.

From that we write the rules and set them up in your store, so new orders are tagged as they arrive. We test the rules on your past orders to see how many would have been flagged, and adjust any that flag too many ordinary customers.

The Basic package covers a first set of simple rules with tags and an email alert. The Standard package adds more signals, a shared review queue, a saved decision note for each order and the past order test. The Premium package tunes the rules using your own chargeback history, adds risk levels and an evidence checklist, and ends with a staff guide and a short handover call.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Treat a flag as a reason to look, not as proof.
- Contact the customer by email when an order looks odd but may be real.
- Record your decision on every flagged order, so patterns appear over time.
- Review the rules after busy seasons, when buying habits change.
- Keep using the fraud checks your payment provider already offers.

**Avoid:**
- Canceling orders on a flag alone, without a look at the details.
- Adding so many rules that nearly every order is flagged.
- Ignoring the alert emails because they arrive too often.
- Sharing customer details in chat or public channels while checking an order.
- Assuming the rules never need a change once they are in place.

## Who this is for

It suits a store owner who has already lost money to a chargeback and wants a repeatable check. It suits a seller who ships high value items and wants a second look before the parcel leaves. It also suits a small team where several people process orders and need one shared standard for what looks risky.

## What we need from you

Send a short note about your past problem orders and, if you can, an export of recent orders marked with the ones that went wrong. Tell us who reviews orders and how quickly they can respond. We never need passwords: access is given as a collaborator, staff or developer user with limited permissions. The flags work on information already in your store, and we do not copy customer details elsewhere.
